post.description:
Provision (or fetch) a deposit address for an end-user.

SUA-gated for every new ``(asset, network)`` request. The call
lands a ``CryptoVaultProvisionRequest`` and returns ``202`` with the
request id; SUA approval triggers the Fireblocks side-effect (vault
create on first wallet for the user, asset-enable on subsequent
wallets — the existing vault is reused). Subsequent calls for the
same ``(tenant, user, asset, network)`` that has already been
approved-and-allocated return the existing deposit address inline.
For ERC20-style assets the response carries a ``gas_dependency``
block with the auto-provisioned gas wallet so the platform can
prompt the user to top up.

**Wrong-network deposits are typically irrecoverable.** The
response includes ``network_code`` (e.g. ``ethereum``, ``tron``)
alongside ``address``. End-users must send funds on the **exact
network the address belongs to**. Sending an asset from a different
chain — for example USDT-TRC20 to an Ethereum address, or
Bitcoin to an EVM address — results in lost funds; we cannot
detect or recover such deposits because they never reach our
custody. Surface ``network_code`` prominently in any deposit UI
your platform builds on top of this endpoint.

deliberately excluded — that bucket holds platform revenue, not
user balance. Pass ``user_id`` to scope the response to a single
end-user (useful for "wallet" pages on the platform UI).

post.description:
Public, provider-agnostic international payout endpoint.

Client / end-user integrations ship only Finogates-domain
identifiers (``beneficiaryId`` + ``bankAccountId``) and the
transaction details (``amount``, ``sourceCurrency``,
``destinationCurrency``). Sender / business identity, full
beneficiary fields, full bank-info fields, destination branch ID,
product routing, and provider selection are all resolved
server-side from records the client pre-creates via:

* ``POST /v1/platform/payees`` *or*
  ``POST /v1/platform/payment-methods/bank`` — saved bank account
  (with ``meta.payout_branch_id`` captured at creation time).
* The platform's SUA-configured Uniteller sender defaults.

Provider-specific fields never leak into this contract. The
response is the standardised :class:`InternationalPayoutRead`
shape (same schema as the equivalent tenant endpoint).

This is the canonical replacement for the deprecated
``POST /v1/platform/international/payouts/process`` route — new
integrations should target ``POST /v1/platform/international/process-payouts``
exclusively.

post.summary: (Legacy) Submit an international payout via the provider-shaped payload
post.description:
**Legacy / provider-shaped endpoint — retained for backward compatibility only.**

This endpoint exposes the underlying Uniteller (More) provider field
names directly (``orderPartnerID``, ``payoutBranchID``,
``payoutCurrency``, …) and was the first public payout surface
shipped on the Platform API. It is retained so existing integrations
do not break, but **new client / end-user integrations should not be
built against it**.

### Why it is being phased out — provider plumbing leaking into your API

The provider-shaped contract forces the integrator to do routing work
that should never have left the server. The two worst offenders are:

* ``product_id`` — the client is asked to pre-select which
  Finogates *product* (rail + provider route) will process the
  payout. That is a backend concern: given the destination corridor
  and the tenant's enabled products, there is exactly one correct
  international-payout product to route through, and the platform
  knows it. Asking the client to discover and pass it is a leak.
* ``payoutBranchID`` — a numeric Uniteller-internal branch id.
  Conceptually it belongs on the saved bank, not on every payout
  call. The new shape persists it on the bank account
  (``meta.payout_branch_id``) and the server reads it from there.

Finogates is moving to a **provider-agnostic, resource-oriented
contract** where the integrator ships only Finogates-domain
identifiers (``beneficiaryId`` + ``bankAccountId``) and the
platform resolves *every* provider concept internally — sender
profile, beneficiary, bank, destination branch, product routing,
and provider selection.

The clean shape is already live on the Tenant API at:

* ``POST /v1/tenant/international/payouts`` — uses
  :class:`InternationalPayoutCreate`, returns
  :class:`InternationalPayoutRead`.

The equivalent endpoint on this Platform API surface
(``POST /v1/platform/international/process-payouts``) is the
canonical replacement for this route. It accepts the same
Finogates-ID-only request body, emits the same standardised
response shape, and removes the ``product_id`` / ``payoutBranchID``
fields from the public contract entirely. Integrators consuming
the Platform API should migrate to that endpoint.

### Client-side vs server-side responsibilities

| Concern              | This (legacy) endpoint | New ``/payouts`` shape |
|----------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Pick the *product*   | **Client** must pass ``product_id`` | Server resolves from rail + corridor |
| Pick the destination *branch* | **Client** must pass ``payoutBranchID`` | Server reads ``meta.payout_branch_id`` from the saved bank |
| Pick the *provider*  | Server (routing matrix) | Server (routing matrix) |
| Pick the *sender profile* | Server (tenant default), client may override via ``sender_id`` | Same — server-resolved |
| Quote FX             | Server (or client passes ``payoutAmount`` for a pre-quoted amount) | Server (or client passes ``destinationAmount``) |
| Reserve / settle ledger | Server | Server |
| Idempotency anchor   | Client — ``orderPartnerID`` | Client — ``reference`` |

### What this endpoint still accepts

Only the **canonical request variant** of ``MorePayoutRequest`` is
accepted here:

| Field | Required | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| ``orderPartnerID``       | ✅ | Caller-supplied reference / idempotency anchor. |
| ``orderCurrency``        | ✅ | ISO-4217 funding-side currency. |
| ``orderAmount``          | ✅ | Amount to debit from the tenant wallet. |
| ``payoutBranchID``       | ✅ | *Leak* — numeric Uniteller branch id from ``GET /v1/platform/international/branches``. Removed on the new shape. |
| ``payoutCurrency``       | ✅ | ISO-4217 recipient-side currency. |
| ``product_id``           | ✅ | *Leak* — UUID of the international payout product. Server-resolved on the new shape. |
| ``payee_payment_method_id`` | ✅ | UUID of a saved payment method that resolves the recipient bank. |
| ``payoutAmount``         | optional | Pre-quoted destination amount; server quotes when omitted. |
| ``sender_id``            | optional | Override the platform's default Uniteller sender profile. |

The **legacy inline shape** (``beneficiary`` + ``bankInfo`` posted
directly on the request) is **rejected** on this Platform endpoint
with HTTP 400 — saved payment methods are mandatory for client API
integrations.

### Behaviour

The request runs through the same orchestration pipeline as the
tenant ``/payouts`` endpoint:

1. ``enforce_product_permission`` — entitlement / Casbin check.
2. ``select_provider`` / ``ProductProvider`` resolution.
3. Ledger reservation (``available`` → ``escrow``) via
   :class:`LedgerPostingService`.
4. Provider call to Uniteller with the resolved sender + saved bank.
5. ``escrow`` → ``clearing`` on success, escrow release on failure.

Status, retry, and reconciliation behave identically to the
successor endpoint.

post.description:
Exchange client credentials for a short-lived JWT access token.

This endpoint implements the **OAuth2 client_credentials** grant:

- Accepts ``client_id`` and ``client_secret`` issued during onboarding
- Returns a JWT scoped to the client's environment (sandbox / production)
- Token lifetime is **24 minutes (1440 seconds)** — re-authenticate when it expires
- IP allowlist is enforced when configured on the client

### Authentication

This endpoint is **unauthenticated** — it is the authentication step itself.

### Mode

The request mode (sandbox / production) is determined by the **server URL**
you call (e.g. ``sandbox-api.finogates.com`` vs ``api.finogates.com``).
The client's environment must match the resolved mode.

### Rate Limiting

Standard rate limits apply.  Repeated authentication failures may trigger
temporary blocks.

post.description:
Submit a payment on the platform — creates the intent **and** executes
it against the resolved provider in a single call (one-shot submit).

This endpoint enables platforms to:

- Initiate a **funding** (deposit from external source into a wallet)
- Initiate a **payout** (withdrawal from a wallet to an external method)
- Initiate a **transfer** (wallet-to-wallet movement)
- Initiate a **relay** (external-to-external pass-through)

The ``intent_type`` field determines which auxiliary fields are required:

| Intent type | Required fields |
|-------------|----------------|
| `funding`   | `product_id`, `payment_method_id` |
| `payout`    | `product_id`, **either** `payee_destination_id` (modern) **or** `payee_payment_method_id` (legacy) |
| `transfer`  | `destination_wallet_id` |
| `relay`     | `payment_method_id`, **either** `payee_destination_id` **or** `payee_payment_method_id` |

For payout / relay flows that use Checkbook auto-deposit, ACH push to a
saved bank, or email-tokenized payouts, pass ``payee_destination_id`` —
that's the canonical model. ``payee_payment_method_id`` remains accepted
for backward compatibility.

The response carries the post-execution intent state. Inspect
``status`` to determine the outcome:

- ``processing`` — provider call is in flight; final state arrives via
  webhook (e.g. ``payment_intent.settled``).
- ``succeeded`` — provider accepted; awaiting settlement webhook.
- ``settled`` — terminal (rare on submit; usually arrives by webhook).
- ``failed`` — terminal; ``failure_reason`` carries a machine-readable
  code (e.g. ``checkbook_returned_R01``).
- ``pending_review`` — an admin approval rule flagged the intent.
  No provider call was made; status will advance via webhook once
  reviewed.

An **idempotency_key** is mandatory to prevent duplicate payments.

get.description:
Return a short-lived hosted add-bank URL the integrator embeds as an
iframe ``src``. The hosted page renders Plaid Link inside the iframe,
exchanges the resulting public token, stores the bank account as a
PaymentMethod, and emits a ``payment_method.bank.added`` webhook to the
platform on success.

### Response
- ``user_id`` — the end user the URL is bound to.
- ``add_bank_url`` — iframe-ready URL with a single-use path token.
- ``expires_at`` — absolute UTC expiry (~10 minutes from now).

### Notification
- On success, the platform receives a ``payment_method.bank.added``
  webhook carrying the linked account data and ``user_id``. This webhook
  is the authoritative success channel — the hosted page does not
  postMessage to the parent window.
- On hosted-page failure (expired/tampered token, validation error)
  no add is attempted and no webhook is fired. Re-call this endpoint
  to mint a fresh URL — there is no refresh.

The URL does NOT carry any provider-specific identifiers (the word
``plaid`` never appears). Treat it as opaque.

post.description:
Replays failed webhook deliveries for the authenticated platform.

Failed deliveries are reset to ``pending`` and the background dispatch
worker is triggered for immediate retry.

### Filters

Provide one or more optional filters to narrow the replay scope:

- ``delivery_id`` — replay a single delivery
- ``event_id`` — replay all failed deliveries for a specific event
- ``endpoint_id`` — replay all failed deliveries for a specific endpoint
- ``limit`` — maximum number of deliveries to replay (default 100, max 500)

If no filters are provided, the most recent failures up to ``limit``
are replayed.

Apply for a virtual bank account ("DDA Account") on behalf of one of
your end users.

**Pre-conditions** — the request fails with 403 unless all are met:
- Your platform has the ``dda_account`` product enabled (request access
  via the standard onboarding flow; SUA admins approve the product
  request in their approvals queue before this endpoint is callable).
- The end user has an **approved** KYC record.
- The end user has at least one **approved** KYB record.

**Lifecycle** — the account is created in ``initiated`` status. A
Finogate administrator manually reviews each application, marks it as
``applied`` once verified, and finally enters the routing / account
numbers issued by the banking partner before flipping the account to
``approved``. Your integration is notified through the outbound
``virtual_bank_account.approved`` webhook (or
``virtual_bank_account.rejected`` on decline) — that event is the
single signal that the account is live and may be surfaced to the end
user. **Until ``approved``, the account must not be used for
transactions, payouts, deposits, or wallet linkage.**

**Idempotency** is enforced two ways:
- An optional ``idempotency_key`` field provides exact request-level
  de-duplication (a duplicate key with a different payload returns 409).
- A partial unique index prevents the same end user from holding two
  non-rejected accounts of the same ``account_type`` for the same
  platform — duplicate attempts return 409.

MorePayoutRequest.title: MorePayoutRequest
MorePayoutRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /tenant/international/payouts/process``.

**Sender is server-managed.** API consumers never need to supply sender /
business-identity fields. Finogates resolves the sender block from the
SUA-configured platform defaults (``Tenant.meta['uniteller_sender_defaults']``)
and injects it into the outbound provider call. This is part of the
Finogates orchestration contract — provider-specific mandatory fields are
enriched server-side, never required from the customer.

The endpoint accepts two shapes:

* **Canonical (preferred)** — ``product_id`` + ``payee_payment_method_id``.
  Routes through ``ensure_tenant_product_entitled`` → ``select_provider``
  → ``reserve_funds`` → ``ensure_payment_method_binding`` → provider call
  → ``move_escrow_to_clearing`` / ``release_escrow``. Beneficiary and bank
  info are loaded from the saved ``PaymentMethod`` (and optionally a
  linked ``InternationalBeneficiary``).
* **Legacy (deprecated)** — inline ``beneficiary`` + ``bankInfo``.
  Bypasses the entitlement / ledger / binding pipeline. New integrations
  MUST use the canonical shape; the legacy shape is retained only to
  avoid breaking the integration that just shipped.

Exactly one of the two shapes must be present.

Internal/advanced fields (not part of the public surface, retained for
backward compatibility):

* ``sender_id`` — explicitly select a saved ``InternationalSender`` row
  instead of falling back to the platform defaults. Tenant-managed by SUA;
  most integrators leave this unset.
* ``sender`` — inline override of the sender block. **Deprecated and
  ignored by default**: server-side enrichment runs whenever the
  enrichment dispatcher returns a populated block, so this field is
  effectively only honored when the platform has no defaults configured.

PlatformVirtualBankAccountCreate.title: PlatformVirtualBankAccountCreate
PlatformVirtualBankAccountCreate.description:
Public platform request shape for ``POST /platform/virtual-bank-accounts``.

Field aliases accept both the spec-style camelCase (``userID``) and
the canonical snake_case so integrators can use whichever they
prefer; documentation should standardise on snake_case.

url.title: Url
url.description: HTTPS URL that will receive webhook POST requests.

events.title: Events
events.description: Individual event types to subscribe to. An empty list subscribes to all events.

event_groups.title: Event Groups
event_groups.description: Event groups to subscribe to (e.g. 'payment', 'wallet'). Expanded into individual event types and merged with events.

description.title: Description
description.description: Optional human-readable description for the webhook endpoint.

PlatformWebhookDeliveryReplayRequest.title: PlatformWebhookDeliveryReplayRequest
PlatformWebhookDeliveryReplayRequest.description:
Replay selector for failed webhook deliveries (platform API).

Provide at least one filter, or omit all to replay up to ``limit``
most-recent failures.

TwilioCredentialsPayload.title: TwilioCredentialsPayload
TwilioCredentialsPayload.description:
Per-user Twilio account credentials supplied by the admin.

All fields are required for full SUA provisioning — the API + Voice
SDK access tokens cannot be issued without ``api_key`` / ``api_secret``
and the three SID fields drive outbound calling and mobile push.
Use ``TwilioCredentialsPatchPayload`` for partial rotation.

VirtualBankAccountType.title: VirtualBankAccountType
VirtualBankAccountType.description:
Account product for virtual bank accounts.

PAYWINT_BUSINESS is the only supported type today; KYC + KYB are
both mandatory and the account stays gated until both pass.
